strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 all-reduce operations sequentially, each preceded by local per-shard scaling (multiply by a[r]/W) and followed by local normalization (divide by a[r]). Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 16 element-wise operations that can be fused. Minimizes code complexity at the cost of maximum dispatch count.

strategies.name: Fused scale-allreduce kernel batching
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all scaling coefficients and fuses scale+clone operations into vectorized operations before each all-reduce, reducing memory traffic. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but eliminates redundant buffer allocations by reusing two ping-pong buffers. Trades dispatch count for memory bandwidth efficiency.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc: Groups the 8 dependent all-reduces into 2 or 4 stages where inner stages batch multiple scale/normalize cycles using tensor views or strides. Potentially reduces effective dispatch overhead by amortizing collective setup costs across multi-level operations. Exploits structural similarity in repeated scale-reduce-normalize pattern.

strategies.name: Pipelined all-reduce with async dispatch
strategies.desc: Overlaps computation (scaling/normalization) of iteration i+1 with communication (all-reduce) of iteration i by pre-computing scaling buffers for multiple iterations. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches but hides local compute latency behind network transfers. Maximizes throughput on large world_size by exploiting collective/compute concurrency.

strategies.name: Coefficient-precomputed single-buffer mutation
strategies.desc:
Allocates a single working buffer and performs all 8 iterations in-place, computing composite scaling factors (product of all intermediate a[r]/W and 1/a[r] terms) to minimize buffer clones. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches but only 2 tensor allocations total (input and working buffer). Optimizes for memory footprint and allocation overhead.
